newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROBSON HOPE TO END ON A WINNG NOTE..
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROBSON HOPE TO END ON A WINNG NOTE..

text.p: Whatever the result of the Spanish Cup final at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday, it will be the last game for both Bobby Robson and Lorenzo Serra Ferrer as coaches of Barcelona and Real Betis.
Neither has confirmed where he will be at the start of next season but it is widely expected that they will be working together at Barcelona.
Robson announced on Thursday that he would not continue as Barcelona's first-team coach.

Rumours persist that, as he has an expensive two-year contract, he will stay at the Catalan club and become general manager, with Ajax Amsterdam coach Louis van Gaal coming in to fill the former England manager's present position.
Serra Ferrer announced on June 20 that he would stay with Real Betis only 10 more days after a disagreement with club president Miguel Ruiz de Lopera.

He is also expected to find employment at Camp Nou, probably as reserve team coach. Ruiz de Lopera was said to have demanded that Serra Ferrer sign an agreement not to move to Cup final opponents Barcelona.
Robson and Serra Ferrer have much in common, should they join forces.
Both made their names by bringing success to unfashionable clubs with few resources at their disposal.
Robson took over at Ipswich Town in 1969 and in the next 13 years took them to victory in both the FA Cup and UEFA Cup as well as second place in the English league in 1981.
Serra Ferrer took charge of Spanish second division Real Mallorca in 1986 and immediately led them into the first divison.
The following year they finished in a club record sixth place. They were relegated in 1988 but Serra Ferrer took them straight back into the top flight.
Nicknamed 'The Wizard', he took over at Real Betis in 1994 and produced similar magic at the Seville club.
Betis were promoted back to the first divison in Serra Ferrer's first year there and since then they have been major contenders for Spanish honours.
The two managers have also seen at close quarters the fickle nature of the Spanish soccer media and fans.

Robson started his year in Barcelona being reviled by both sets of pundits for his unspectacular but effective tactics and his import of foreign players at the expense of talented products of the Barcelona youth system.

However, in recent weeks -- in the wake of Barcelona's European Cup Winners's Cup triumph, making the final of the Copa del Rey and a strong second-place finish in the league -- even his harshest critics have grudgingly admitted that they were wrong.
By contrast, public opinion has run against Serra Ferrer. His former god-like status in Andalusia has been severely diminished after his recent discussions with Barcelona.
What is widely perceived as a good career move throughout the rest of the soccer world is openly viewed as treachery by Betis supporters.
Despite their imminent departures, both men are determined to leave their present jobs on a winning note.
"I know it's going to be my last game on the bench of the first team and it is very important for me to say goodbye with a win," Robson said.
His sentiments are no doubt echoed by Serra Ferrer. The two men have more in common than just hair turned grey by the stresses of standing on the sidelines.
